paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between iteration number and loss for different model configurations. The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration”, is linear, ranging from 0 to 140000, with tick labels every 20000 units. The y-axis, labeled “Loss”, is linear, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at 0.1 intervals. A purple line labeled “Vanilla” begins at approximately 3.3 at an iteration of 0 and decreases to approximately 2.6 at iteration 140000, exhibiting a rapid decline initially followed by a flattening trend. A blue line labeled “StrmLLM (n=64)” starts at approximately 3.2 at iteration 0 and decreases to approximately 2.6 at iteration 140000, following a similar pattern of initial rapid decline and subsequent stabilization. An orange line labeled “SepLLM (n=64)” begins at approximately 3.1 at iteration 0 and decreases to approximately 2.55 at iteration 140000, also demonstrating a rapid decrease followed by a leveling off. A green line labeled “SepLLM (n=64, H)” starts at approximately 3.1 at iteration 0 and ends at approximately 2.55 at iteration 140000, with a comparable decreasing trend. A magenta line labeled “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” starts at approximately 3.1 at iteration 0 and decreases to approximately 2.55 at iteration 140000 and follows a similar pattern. Finally, a dark blue line labeled “SepLLM (n=128)” starts at approximately 3.1 at iteration 0 and reaches approximately 2.6 at iteration 140000, exhibiting a decrease similar to the other lines.
